newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firmer, barge and cargo premiums steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firmer, barge and cargo premiums steady.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices were firmer on Tuesday, matching gains on benchmark gas oil futures.
Traders said business was still fairly thin with the dollar's strength dampening demand from the key German market for barges and ample Russian 0.2 sulphur supplies keeping cargo buyers relaxed.

Premiums for prompt 0.2 sulphur cargoes held steady around August IPE $$1.50/+$2 a tonne cif NWE with trade reported for a very prompt piece at around $2.75 over on Monday. But the recent contango on premiums to early August turned into a small backwardation with a healthier supply seen from Ventspils.
Around five Russian cargo are scheduled to load by July 25, trade sources said.
Diesel cargo premiums were holding firm after a flurry of trade on Monday. Most of the business was for August delivery but a prompt cargo was sold into Bordeaux at around Aug IPE +$3.50 a tonne.
Prompt deliveries valued around August IPE +$4.50 cif Le Havre.
Flushing diesel barges were traded a couple of times at August IPE +$4 a tonne fob with Rotterdam liftings commanding a $1 premium.

Heating oil barge trade was quite. Traders said that with the firmer dollar stifling demand from Germany and loading delays in Rotterdam meaning many players would be getting oil later than expected, most interest was focused on early August liftings.
Brokers said the loading delays at the jointly owned BP, Texaco Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam have been caused by hefty nominations for loading on the 16th.
"Some of the barges have been given deferred loading dates in order to avoid demurrage costs but all will get there oil," a broker said.

Prompt barges talked steady around August IPE +$1/+$1.50 fob ARA with early August premiums 25 to 50 cents firmer at August IPE +75 cents to +$1 per tonne fob ARA with second half August liftings around August IPE +50 cents/+$1.
